key_insight: A diffusion-based generative model that jointly models multiple cardiovascular biomarkers to synthesize, impute, and harmonize cross-modal physiological signals, preserving clinically relevant dynamics and cross-modal dependencies.
problem_solved: Addresses the challenge of sparse, heterogeneous and partially missing multimodal cardiovascular monitoring data by enabling realistic cross-modal generation and imputation so models can be trained and validated without requiring fully paired recordings.
method: Adapt a diffusion generative framework for multimodal time-series with modality-specific encoders/decoders and a shared latent fusion to capture cross-modal dependencies.
Train conditional generation and imputation objectives so the model can synthesize missing modalities, translate between modalities (e.g., ECG ↔ PPG), and preserve clinical biomarkers.
Evaluate fidelity and clinical utility via signal reconstruction metrics and downstream tasks (e.g., arrhythmia/risk prediction) to demonstrate improved robustness and realism.
impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners to augment scarce multimodal cardiovascular datasets, perform robust cross-modal imputation, and simulate monitoring scenarios—reducing the need for fully paired clinical recordings and improving downstream model performance.
visual_elements: Model schematic: modality-specific encoders → shared latent fusion → diffusion-based generator → modality decoders (showing conditional/imputation paths).
Before/after examples: aligned waveform panels (ECG, PPG, blood pressure) showing real vs. generated/imputed signals with preserved biomarkers.
Cross-modal attention/correlation heatmap: visualizing learned dependencies between biomarkers across modalities.
Bar/line chart: quantitative gains on reconstruction and downstream task metrics (e.g., AUROC, MSE) comparing baseline vs. joint diffusion model.
